agent-management: Everything about riders (called agents in code): new rider applications, profiles, daily attendance and holidays, and how they are paid (salary type or per-parcel commission). Used by ops and HR.
g-mode: A restricted super-user area for fixing things the normal flow can't: reset an agent's login throttle, resolve stuck baskets or orders, regenerate an order's invoice, force-approve urgent requests, or log in as another user to see their problem.
global_layout: Screens shown outside the main dashboard: first-time onboarding and choosing which hub you are working in.
invoice: Money a hub collected: consignments whose COD is ready to deposit, and the hub's deposit submissions.
invoices: Finance's area: generate and pay merchant invoices, approve hub deposits, hub money dashboards, transaction history, agent delivery allowance and reconciliation of claims.
landlord: Owners of the premises Carrybee rents for its hubs, used for paying rent.
merchant: Sellers on the platform: their businesses, corporate accounts, KYC profiles, store approvals, store location checks, payout account changes and discount requests.
oms: The day-to-day parcel operation: pickup requests and orders, hub drop-off, first-mile processing, baskets, central sorting and sub-sort, delivery orders, returns, QC approvals, and exception queues (no-entry, incomplete, lost, missing/extra).
petty-cash: Hub expenses and rent claims, approved step by step (ops head → HR → audit → accounts) and withdrawn by OTP.
qr-campaign-management: Referral QR codes and short links used to bring new sellers to Carrybee, with visit tracking.
rating-management: How customers and sellers rate riders, with per-hub summaries and weekly trends.
reports: Downloadable CSV reports: baskets, consignments, merchants and custom reports.
run-management: Agent trips: pickup runs, delivery runs, transfer runs between hubs, return-to-merchant runs and customer return runs. Create, assign, track and close them.
system-setting: Staff notifications and the push notification center for sending messages to users.
users: Staff accounts and who can do what: users, teams, departments, roles and permissions.
warehouse: The physical network: hubs (warehouses), regions, clusters, routes, linehauls between hubs, zone polygons on the map, and the hub ledger.
top level: Pages not inside a menu group: dashboards (business insights, hub performance), activity log, fraud reports, POD printing, PTN racks, unclosed runs, login and logout.

Pages that open as a popup over the current screen (Next.js intercepting routes), such as the profile, request pickup and change password dialogs.
developers-api: Documentation, credentials and webhook setup for sellers who connect their own shop or system to Carrybee.
top level: Everything a seller does day to day: dashboard, orders, pickups, stores, customers, invoices, payments, team members and alerts. Also signup, login and public order tracking.
Revenue recognition (merchant invoices), legal order export, business and merchant lists, and consignment reports.
